answer.rationale: Current constraints bind harder than any single memory. The line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and a hard 14-day expiry makes switch_primary_vendor (memory_c2) the highest-variance option: memory_c2 records a favorable outcome but says nothing about the volume, criticality, or ramp window of that switch, and a migration executed under a two-week cliff with zero inventory buffer risks the delivery-risk half of the objective to chase the cost half. defer_decision is not available in the form memory_c5 describes: that memory concerns a non-critical service that fell back to month-to-month terms, whereas this contract does not auto-renew, so deferral is a supply lapse, not a preserved option. add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right structural fix for concentration risk but delivers little of an 18% in-year cut and does not resolve the expiring primary contract, so it is the wrong use of a single decision slot this cycle. That leaves the renewal lever. The incumbent has refused to reopen price *this cycle*, which forecloses the straight benchmarking play in memory_c4 but not the term-structure play in memory_c6, where a longer commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope. Price-per-unit and contract duration are distinct levers, and a refusal on one is not a refusal on the other. So I intend to negotiate terms at renewal: trade duration and volume commitment for unit cost, structured as a guarded step rather than a full multi-year lock. Why I want memory_c6 and memory_c2 verified: memory_c6 is now the load-bearing memory for my chosen action, and the consolidated summary is outcome-only with no counterfactual, no record of what duration was committed, whether the volume floor was achievable, or what exit provisions existed. If that discount required a volume commitment above what a line at 94% can safely guarantee, the memory argues against itself here. memory_c2 is the strongest competing option and I want to know the switch's scale and ramp time before I discard it; if it was a like-for-like component with a short qualification path, switching may deserve the slot after all. I am not verifying memory_c4 because the current situation already overrides it, nor memory_c3/memory_c5, which lose on fit rather than on evidence quality. Two flags I am carrying forward rather than resolving. First, the 18% mandate may simply not be reachable this cycle without accepting delivery risk or scope loss; if the term-structure play yields materially less, the honest output is a partial cut plus an explicit gap, not a stretch commitment that shows up later as expedite fees, quality escapes, or a missed volume floor triggering clawback. Second, every one of these memories is a success record with survivorship built in, no failed sourcing decisions were consolidated, so the inherited base rate is optimistic and I am discounting accordingly. Guarded scale means: shortest term that still triggers volume pricing, an explicit exit or repricing window, and no commitment to a volume floor above current sustained throughput, which keeps a second-source or vendor-switch decision live at the next review instead of foreclosing it.
